name: @merit/api
description: The /api/v1 surface API_CONTRACT specifies. Railway services: api (public origin) and api-admin (ADMIN_ORIGIN), one codebase deployed twice per ADR-083.
//: IT DECLARED NO RUNTIME DEPENDENCY UNTIL ADR-100 AND FASTIFY'S ABSENCE WAS THE FENCE RATHER THAN THE RULING. ADR-083 ruling 3 chose the framework and deliberately did not install it: the version lives in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `catalog:` block, which session 144 did not hold, and `.npmrc`'s `save-exact` plus VG-12 make a version a human approves once rather than a caret. ADR-100 is that admission -- every package named, every resolution checked for a registry entry carrying a `sha512` integrity hash, `pnpm audit --audit-level=low` run and the closure delta stated -- and it is why `"fastify": "catalog:"` is below. THERE IS NO `build` SCRIPT AND THERE MUST NOT BE ONE. `CI-06/gate-inventory` probes every apps/*/package.json for that key and requires it ABSENT, because CI-07's row reads through an artifact that does not exist; a build script makes that gate fail on good news. Fastify 5 needs none, which ADR-083 section 5 measured and which `pnpm run start` now demonstrates rather than predicts: `node --experimental-strip-types src/index.ts` serves the registry with nothing compiled.
//dependencies: `@merit/affiliate`, `@merit/kyc` AND `@merit/psp` ARE WORKSPACE DEPENDENCIES AND NOT CATALOG ONES, so `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is untouched and VG-12 is asked to admit nothing: the only lines `pnpm-lock.yaml` gains are these importers' own. `.npmrc` sets `node-linker=isolated`, which makes an undeclared import unresolvable at run time; **AND ALSO AT BUILD TIME, WHICH THIS KEY GOT WRONG UNTIL ADR-120.** It said `tsc` resolves such an import `happily through the workspace`. ADR-117 section 5 measured that from this very package and reported it FALSE -- `error TS2307: Cannot find module '@merit/db'`, with no `paths` mapping anywhere in the tree -- and rowed the repair as owed by whoever next held this file. That is this session, so the sentence is corrected here rather than left standing beside the entry that refuted it. THE CONCLUSION IT WAS DRAWN FOR SURVIVES AND IS STRONGER THAN IT WAS: the declaration is not merely where the dependency is recorded, it is THE ONLY PLACE THE CAPABILITY CAN BE ACQUIRED, which is what makes `RI-08`'s manifest check the whole control rather than half of one. `ls apps/api/node_modules/@merit` is how the linkage was measured rather than assumed. **`@merit/db` IS HERE AS OF ADR-120 AND ITS ARRIVAL IS A RULING RATHER THAN A LINE.** Session 219 found its absence, ADR-112 removed the obstacle ADR-109 clause 3 named, and sessions 218 and 220 each reached this line from a slice whose subject was something else and each correctly declined: the admission is an authority change on the deployable that serves the whole public surface and not a side effect of a checkout slice. **IT IS ALSO AN ENTRY IN `DB_ADMITTED`**, the first that list has ever carried, so this line alone does not buy the capability: with the line here and that list empty `RI-08` fails and `CI-01` is red, which is exactly what ADR-117 section 4 designed the quiet line to cost. See `src/db.ts`, ADR-120, ADR-117, ADR-113 and ADR-109.
